long_biography.plain_text:
Businessman Bernard Cox brought experience in outsourced services to a courier venture proposed by advertising entrepreneur Duan Coetzee. Coetzee had spotted an opening while handling a client's brief and approached Cox, whose existing businesses covered cleaning and plant hire. Their collaboration combined the new delivery concept with Cox's knowledge of running service operations.

Cox emphasised speed and quality when explaining Berco's expansion. Its courier operation used satellite tracking to locate parcels, detect interference with truck doors and identify vehicles leaving designated areas. He also favoured selective acquisitions: expansion into other markets would depend on finding businesses that met the group's standards.
